meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common law heritage; offshore special territory with locally enacted statutes; territorial income tax system, no VAT, no capital gains tax)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: UK–Gibraltar taxation integration via the Income Tax Act 2010 (territorial extension; ELP treated as tax transparent)
Limited UK double taxation arrangements extended to Gibraltar where expressly stated by Order in Council
OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS participant (Gibraltar applies country-by-country reporting exchange standards)
UK–EU–Spain Framework on Gibraltar (political agreement of 31 December 2020; treaty signed 12 April 2023, pending ratification; relevant to future market-access and services passporting)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (as amended); Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism) Regulations 2011 (as amended); Criminal Finances Act 2019; Sanctions Act 2019; Financial Services (Investment and Fiduciary Services) Act 2018; Limited Partnerships Act 2019 (Part 8, Beneficial Ownership); Companies (Central Register of Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2017; GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes (current edition); UN Financial Sanctions Regulations (Gibraltar).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed corporate services provider / fiduciary of the general partner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies House Gibraltar (Registrar of Companies) or originating foreign registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies of the individual general partner and all 25%+ beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address and source-of-funds affidavit for each 25%+ beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or regulated home bank confirming address

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions) or direct dispatch under GFSC guidance

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence before appointment of the general partner; screening of all named partners, beneficial owners and directors against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Gibraltar Domestic Sanctions List; PEP status determination at onboarding and continuous transaction monitoring; enhanced due diligence for PEPs, family members and close associates under GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes; mandatory filing of beneficial ownership details in the Central Register for any person holding more than 25% ownership or control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies House (Registrar of Companies); name reservation and incorporation e-services portal at https://www.companieshouse.gi
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official working language is English; registered names must use Latin-script alphanumeric characters (A-Z, 0-9) with limited punctuation; no translation or transliteration is required for English-language names; the name of an Exempted Limited Partnership must end with 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.' or 'LP' to denote limited liability; the Registrar may refuse names that are misleading as to legal form, offensive, or insufficiently distinguishable from names already on the Register.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are valid for 30 days from the date of clearance and are not automatically renewable; if incorporation is not completed within the window, a fresh application and statutory fee are required. Upon rejection, the applicant may submit written representations to the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the notice; the Registrar will issue a reasoned determination. An adverse determination may be challenged by way of judicial review proceedings before the Supreme Court of Gibraltar within 3 months, with further appeal to the Gibraltar Court of Appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible as a registered office address only when provided by a licensed fiduciary or corporate services provider maintaining a physical office in Gibraltar; a virtual address alone cannot establish tax residence or economic substance. Commercial substance for the micro-SaaS ELP is evidenced by the local registered agent, the place of effective management and control of the general partner, and, where Gibraltar tax residence is sought, the holding of board meetings and decision-making in Gibraltar.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 3% to 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a Low-Risk-Standard AML tier micro-SaaS ELP; inspections are conducted by the GFSC and by licensed registered agents under AML/CFT supervision; incremental risk applies if the ELP onboards high-risk customers, transacts with sanctioned jurisdictions, or fails to maintain a coherent substance file.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act 1991, as amended by the Limited Partnerships (Amendment) Act 2014 and the Exempted Limited Partnerships Regulations 2014; ss. 4 (constitution), 5 (general partner), 6 (registration), 7 (register of limited partnerships) and 8A (exempt status).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Registry Division, Financial Services Commission, Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form ELP-01 — Application for Registration of an Exempted Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Partnership contributions may be cash or in-kind, may be deferred, and are governed by the Limited Partnership Agreement. No escrow account requirement is imposed by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST GENERAL PARTNER RESOLUTION: The General Partner of the Exempted Limited Partnership resolves: (1) to approve the formation and designation as exempt; (2) to subscribe for, pay or contribute the initial partnership capital as stated in the Partnership Agreement; (3) to adopt the registered office at [Address], Gibraltar; (4) to appoint [Name] as General Partner and [Name] as Limited Partner; (5) to authorize the General Partner to execute Form ELP-01 and all ancillary filings; (6) to appoint a compliance officer and AML officer; and (7) to authorize the opening of bank and merchant payment accounts with Paddle or Lemon Squeezy alongside all documents needed to give effect to this resolution. This resolution takes effect immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry — Name Availability Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name enquiry application through the registry portal or by letter to confirm that the proposed partnership name is distinguishable, not misleading, and not prohibited under the Limited Partnerships Act. Where available, request a name reservation. Retain the acknowledgement for submission with the registration form.
required_dossiers: Cover letter specifying proposed exempt limited partnership status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a revised name application or submit a written representation to the Registrar of Companies seeking a review of the rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar licensed corporate services provider and Gibraltar notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Limited Partnership Agreement reflecting the capital contributions, profit-sharing, management powers, exempt designation, and registered office. Execute the agreement by the General Partner and Limited Partner, notarize signatures, and deliver the executed deed to the registered agent for registration support.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of general and limited partners
Proof of residential or business address for each partner
Consent of the Gibraltar registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registered agent queries the agreement, amend the relevant clauses and resubmit for notarization; any costly reissuance of consent letters is coordinated by the registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Registration Application to Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form ELP-01 online or in person at the Registry Division together with the certified copy of the executed Limited Partnership Agreement, the registered office consent, and the general partner information. Pay the prescribed registration fee and retained duty, if any, and obtain a stamped receipt.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of executed Limited Partnership Agreement
General Partner registered details (name, address, capacity)
Firm check sheet or covering letter from the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond through the registered agent within 14 calendar days, clarify discrepancies, and file any corrective or supplementary documents accepted by the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Registration and Entry into Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval by the Registrar, the partnership is entered into the Register of Limited Partnerships and issued a Certificate of Registration. Verify the registered details, legal form, exempt status, and the date of registration before relying on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of the Exempted Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For certificate errors, submit a written correction request to the Registry Division with supporting evidence; the certificate will be reissued after administrative verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Compliance Officer and Establishment of Statutory Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar licensed corporate services provider acting as registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the statutory register at the registered office in Gibraltar, appoint a compliance officer and money laundering reporting officer, and file the initial beneficial ownership statement under the GDPR-compliant Gibraltar beneficial ownership regime. Obtain signed declarations from the General Partner and Limited Partner.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry or Financial Services Commission identifies a deficiency, the registered agent will correct the registers and resubmit the beneficial ownership statement within the statutory cure period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board supervises this lightweight productivity cloud software activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — activity does not require a manufacturing permit, operating license, or regulated financial/services license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — 100% office-based software-as-a-service activity with no construction or industrial operation; mandatory EIA not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous air emissions generated. Comply with the Wastes Act 2016 (Gibraltar) and, where relevant, the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment regime for disposal of any office hardware or server equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Minimum clearance required: fire safety certificate for the occupied office, structural load confirmation from Building Control for the leased premises, DSE workstation risk assessment, electrical appliance testing, and general occupational safety inspection under the Health and Safety at Work Act (Gibraltar).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, H.M. Government of Gibraltar (official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/tax-customs). For any optional UK connection, HMRC remains a separate competent authority; no HMRC registration is triggered by Gibraltar tax registration alone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the ELP under the Gibraltar Limited Partnerships Act 2019 with Companies House Gibraltar; obtain the Gibraltar Limited Partnership number. Step 2: File any liability notification with the Income Tax Office only if the ELP or its partners carry on a taxable activity deriving Gibraltar-source income; the general partner normally files. Step 3: Receive an Income Tax Office Assessment/Tax Reference number for the chargeable partners. Step 4: Non-resident foreign partners with no Gibraltar activity will not receive a Gibraltar TIN; retain the ELP registration certificate, partnership deed, and foreign tax residence certificate. No Gibraltar VAT ID exists because Gibraltar has no VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; Territorial_Scope. The ELP is statutorily tax-transparent for Gibraltar Income Tax Act purposes; income is allocated to partners. Non-resident partners are taxable in Gibraltar only on Gibraltar-source income or a trade carried on in Gibraltar; no entity-level Gibraltar income tax is imposed on the ELP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar has no check-the-box or entity-classification election; transparency is statutory. For U.S. federal tax purposes, eligible ELPs may be classified under Treasury Reg. section 301.7701-3 by Form 8832, but that election has no Gibraltar tax effect. Hybrid mismatch risks are to be analyzed under the UK TIOPA 2010 Part 6A rules; no Gibraltar-specific mitigation election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No_General_Indirect_Tax_System; Gibraltar is outside the EU VAT area and applies only selective customs/import duty and excise on specific physical goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable for SaaS: no VAT/GST registration threshold in Gibraltar. A physical-goods importer/excise operator may need a customs/excise registration, but this does not apply to the micro-SaaS subscription service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Gibraltar does not maintain a real-time fiscal clearance, CTC e-invoicing, API submission, or digital stamping mandate. Any e-invoices or sales-tax reports from Paddle/Lemon Squeezy are issued under foreign merchant-of-record obligations, not under Gibraltar law.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in Gibraltar: no positive VAT/GST is chargeable, so there is no 0% export VAT claim or refund mechanism. Cross-border SaaS supplies are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax. In a separate UK/EU VAT context, the supplier would apply place-of-supply rules; that is not a Gibraltar export zero-rating event.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No Gibraltar VAT clawback can arise. False declarations to the Commissioner of Income Tax are penalised under the Income Tax Act 2010, as amended, by interest, penalties, and criminal sanctions. The exposure is therefore in the source/tax-residency documentation: disruptive tax misdeclarations may lead to a reopening of the ELP's partnership status, UK GAAR or hybrid mismatch counteraction, and possible strike-off by the Companies House Registrar.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) acts as the integrated banking, AML and financial-services supervisor and as the de facto monetary-regime administrator for Gibraltar; HM Government of Gibraltar is the issuing authority of the Gibraltar pound (GIP), which is pegged at par (1:1) with GBP; the Bank of England and HM Treasury remain the anchor monetary and exchange-control authorities for the sterling zone, with UK exchange controls repealed since 1979.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full liberalisation applies to both current-account and capital-account transactions. GIP is redeemable at par into GBP on demand and functions as a fully convertible sterling-zone token currency. Non-resident partners of the Exempted Limited Partnership may inject capital, receive distributions, and repatriate profits without Gibraltarian withholding tax or exchange-control approval, because the ELP is fiscally transparent and profits are taxable only at partner level. Residual hurdles are documentary only: CRS/FATCA self-certifications, source-of-wealth evidence, and, where tax-transparent treatment is sought, a Commissioner of Income Tax (CFM) non-residency ruling confirming that the ELP has no Gibraltar-sourced profits and no permanent establishment in Gibraltar. No central-bank consent is required for dividends, capital withdrawals, or intra-group funding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or conversion obligation exists in Gibraltar or the UK. There is no repatriation time window, no mandatory conversion ratio (effectively 0 percent), and no central-bank settlement requirement for software subscription revenue received via Paddle or Lemon Squeezy. Settlement payouts in GBP, EUR, or USD may be held indefinitely in the ELP's multi-currency accounts; banks may simply tag settlement receipts by provenance for GFSC AML transparency purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (GBP/GIP base) plus segregated Capital Escrow Account for partner capital injections
Operational and treasury services account (GBP, EUR, USD) with FX desk-linked settlement
Operational account requiring private-banking minimum assets; not structured as a bare capital-escrow current account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: HSBC UK Bank plc (FCA-regulated UK clearing counterparty at GIP/GBP parity)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational clearing current account (GBP) with SWIFT and multi-currency pockets for correspondent rails

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: HIGH for FCA-licensed UK EMIs and neo-banks (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Currencycloud) and for merchant-of-record PSPs (Paddle Ltd, Lemon Squeezy), which routinely on-board Gibraltar-registered ELPs using a UK-standard KYC pack. Feasibility: MEDIUM for EEA-licensed EMIs (e.g., Payoneer and EU providers) because Gibraltar's automatic EEA financial-services passporting ceased after the Brexit transition and most EU EMIs require a UK branch or treat Gibraltar as a restricted registration territory. Feasibility: LOW for non-EEA offshore digital EMIs and crypto-based payment platforms, which are either unsupported by GFSC-licensed banks or create an unacceptable AML counterparty mismatch. Legal constraint: any entity issuing e-money or holding payments for Gibraltar persons on a commercial basis must be authorised under the Gibraltar Financial Services Act 2019 or rely on an applicable UK/EU transitional passport; using an unlicensed offshore EMI as the ELP's sole operating account would violate GFSC AML expectations and jeopardise the primary bank relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar banks' default policy requires at least one General Partner or director of the ELP to attend a physical interview at the bank or with a GFSC-licensed corporate services provider when onboarding a first-time non-resident partnership. In practice, a remotely managed ELP with a Low-Risk Standard micro-SaaS profile can satisfy KYC through the approved introducer route: the CSP certifies identity, address, source of wealth, and executes a live video interview, and the bank treats that introduced pack as face-to-face equivalent. Pure remote opening with no Gibraltar nexus and no regulated introducer is not viable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident, pass-through offshore ELP with a UK/GI dual flag and no visible operating footprint triggers shell-company and substance-verification risk under GFSC AML Guidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: original Certificate of Limited Partnership from the Gibraltar Registry; executed partnership agreement; GFSC beneficial-ownership register extract; letter from the local CSP confirming registered office and AML oversight; Economic Substance Act assessment confirming no tax-abusive structure; CFM non-residency tax-treatment letter; 12-month revenue forecast and Paddle/Lemon Squeezy contracts demonstrating real SaaS operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contribution from an offshore partner bank outside the UK/EEA without corroborating documentation, creating a source-of-funds red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: 12 months of bank statements from the remitting partner's regulated bank; professional net-worth statement and source-of-wealth letter; capital-contribution agreement referencing the ELP escrow ledger; notarised or CSP-certified passports; CRS self-certification; confirmation that remitters are not PEPs and pass sanctions screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring card-not-present revenue from third-party aggregators (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) interpreted as payments-velocity, receivable-factoring, or sub-merchant boarding risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: Merchant of Record agreements with Paddle Ltd and Lemon Squeezy; PSP processing attestations and PCI-DSS AOC; three settlement-cycle payout statements; chargeback and refund statistics below 0.5 percent; commercial rationale for MoR use (EU VAT, global tax compliance); committed monthly volume forecast; signed declaration that no sub-merchants are boarded.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex legal-owner chain (holding corporation over ELP over payment accounts) raising unknown-layer or nominee-control concerns and incomplete UBO visualisation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: group organisational chart with every legal entity and ownership percentage; certificates of good standing for each holding entity; UBO register extracts for each jurisdiction; sanctions and PEP screening reports for all natural persons; signed declaration of no nominee arrangements; consolidated CVs and proof of address for each UBO; written undertaking that the ELP will not process third-party payments and that all SaaS subscriptions are end-consumer transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the partner's bank sends a SWIFT MT103 to the Gibraltar receiving bank (or its UK correspondent at parity) with ISO 20022 purpose code CABB (capital injection) and the narrative CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - ELP GB__GI__KY_ELP__ISIC_6201_02_CONSUMER_MICRO_SAAS. The wire must reference the ELP name exactly as registered to permit automated posting to the Capital Escrow Account. The receiving bank verifies against the onboarding mandate and may request the capital-contribution resolution and source-of-funds pack for any single transfer above GBP 10,000 or for aggregated linked flows. USD and EUR contributions are credited to the multi-currency incoming account and may be converted into GIP at the interbank 1:1 peg via the bank's FX desk. No central-bank validation or import/export authorisation is required; the bank's compliance check and UBO documentation are the only gatekeepers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For SaaS suppliers the ELP will use: (i) UK Faster Payments or CHAPS for GBP vendors and recurring disbursements; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer with IBAN for EU vendors (cloud, media, marketing); (iii) US ACH, Fedwire, or MT103 via correspondent for USD vendors (US data centres and ad platforms); (iv) SWIFT MT103 with purpose code MULT or services rendered plus a commercial invoice for residual cross-border vendor payments; and (v) a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700/MT400) only where a vendor contractually requires bank-backed settlement, which is atypical for a micro-SaaS. Paddle and Lemon Squeezy settle through SEPA, ACH, or Faster Payments into the ELP's operating account using their payout ledger references; all outbound payments are subject to an internal disbursement matrix requiring two-person authorisation above GBP 5,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX conversion at the 1:1 GIP/GBP peg across all treasury balances.
Outright plain-vanilla FX forwards (tenors up to 12 months) with the GFSC-licensed relationship bank for USD/GBP and EUR/GBP exposure.
FX swaps (two-leg notional exchange and re-exchange) for staggered conversion of monthly subscription revenue.
Cross-currency swaps permissible for debt or hedge-designation flows, though not applicable to the equity-funded pass-through ELP base case.
Vanilla OTC FX options (purchased puts and calls) under the Financial Services Act 2019, subject to eligible-counterparty assessment.
NDFs are not available or necessary because the open GIP/GBP market and full convertibility make non-deliverable forwards an unsuitable instrument.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registration Renewal and Return (Form AR-ELP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following the anniversary of the ELP's initial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GIP 10 per day up to a maximum of GIP 200; continuing default for two consecutive years leads to administrative strike-off of the ELP from the Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Owners (UBO Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies – Beneficial Ownership Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after each anniversary of registration and upon any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal offence with fines up to GIP 5,000 and daily default fines of GIP 500; officers may be disqualified for deliberate non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit applies if the ELP exceeds two of the following: annual turnover above GIP 10,200,000, total assets above GIP 5,100,000, or average employees above 50; otherwise full statutory audit exemption is available.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Gibraltar, alternatively FRS 102 (Gibraltar GAAP) for small entities; internal accounts must still present a true and fair view.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must maintain an up-to-date beneficial ownership register at the registered office and file an annual confirmation with the Registrar within 14 days after the anniversary of registration; any change of registrable beneficial owner must be submitted within 14 days of the change.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat corporate income tax rate (Income Tax Act 2010, as amended; effective 1 July 2019 for all Gibraltar-resident companies and for partnerships in respect of Gibraltar-source profits).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Exempted Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent: no Gibraltar tax is levied at the entity level; profits are assessed only in the hands of partners. A non-resident partner is not chargeable in Gibraltar on income accruing outside Gibraltar. Gibraltar levies no VAT, no capital gains tax, no inheritance or wealth tax, and no annual capital duty. Capital allowances on qualifying software and server infrastructure are available at statutory rates.
